new.n: Calligan gold legend, Lizard settlement creek farm
new.pl: E half of sec. 2, Lizard Twp (T90N R31W), Pocahontas County: the 1856 Calligan family claim on Lizard Creek (1904 county history)
new.v: Gold coins, dust and nuggets (family lore)
new.st: Patrick Calligan, a single man in the first Lizard Creek settlement, was killed in August 1856 when his wagon of brick upset in a gully; his was the first death in the county. Family lore said he always carried gold coins in a belt and had a store of gold dust and nuggets that vanished after his death. In 1935 a spiritualist claimed $50,000 might be buried on the old Calligan farm, and the owner of that time made an extensive search. Nothing was reported found.
new.t: Story only in strength: the treasure rests on family lore and a 1935 spiritualist claim, and the 1904 county history tells the accident and the claim without any gold. Both 1935 items are the same local news week, so one source. Private farm: ask permission.
src: Humboldt Independent 30 Apr 1935 p1 'Is Long Missing Treasure Buried on Lizard Farm?' (Newspapers.com image 135768)
Flickinger, Pioneer History of Pocahontas County (1904) pp.157-159, 653 (archive.org cu31924028914335)
pinev: Pin on the E half of sec. 2 T90N R31W, the Calligan family claim of 1856-58 per the 1904 county history; the 1930s owner is not yet checked against a plat (about 500 m).
